note: Urgency accuracy is null because the current classifier contract does not emit urgency.

results.text: Every organization admin is receiving alerts meant only for our workspace.
The CSV uploader accepts the file, then creates zero feedback records without an error.
Filtering to Critical feedback returns Low urgency items as well.
The confidence score is saved as 82 instead of 0.82, so everything looks certain.
Two reviewers can overwrite each other’s category changes without any warning.
The dashboard total drops whenever I select a product area, even though the matching rows remain visible.
A five-row CSV created nine feedback items after I retried a failed upload.
The system marked a legal threat as Praise because the message ended with “thanks.”
Guest reviewers can open organization settings by changing the URL manually.
Slack alerts contain the summary from a different feedback item.
Search stops returning results when the query contains an apostrophe.
The weekly chart labels Monday’s feedback under the previous week.
After accepting a classification, the item remains in Needs Review until I log out.
A malformed model response leaves the item stuck on Classifying forever.
CSV rows containing emoji are imported with the feedback text cut off.
The exported report includes feedback that was deleted yesterday.
Inviting a teammate sends the magic link to the previous address entered.
The dashboard says there are 14 negative items, but the filtered table contains 11.
Bulk reclassifying selected items changes unselected rows too.
Searching for “API” returns every item because the term appears in hidden metadata.
The AI summary invents a refund request that is not present in the original feedback.
Intercom webhook events are processed out of order and an older reply replaces the latest text.
Uploading a valid file named feedback.final.csv is rejected as an unsupported format.
The organization switcher changes the name in the header but keeps the previous workspace data.
Add a webhook that fires only after a human accepts the AI classification.
Could the dashboard show how often reviewers override each category?
Let me assign review items to a teammate with a due date.
Please remember the CSV column mapping for the next upload.
We need multilingual classification for Hindi and English feedback in one workspace.
Allow read-only guests to view dashboards without seeing submitter emails.
Add an exact phrase option alongside the current fuzzy search.
Can exports include the original text and every reviewer correction?
A release marker on the sentiment chart would make trend changes easier to explain.
Support keyboard shortcuts for accept, edit, and next in the review queue.
Let users preview rejected CSV rows and download them for correction.
I would like a second model to review only low-confidence classifications.
Please add SCIM provisioning for larger organizations.
Could filters be shared through a URL without making them public?
Add Microsoft Teams as an alert destination.
Let us break down urgency by product area on the dashboard.
It would be useful to merge duplicate feedback before review.
Please accept TSV files in addition to CSV.
Allow admins to edit the category descriptions shown to the model.
We need temporary guest access that expires automatically.
Add negative keywords so saved searches can exclude known noise.
Could scheduled exports be delivered to an S3 bucket?
Show confidence distribution rather than only the average confidence.
Let reviewers add an explanation when they override the AI.
Long feedback is shown in one unbroken paragraph, making review slow.
The upload progress bar reaches 100% before validation starts, which makes the page look finished.
Confidence is displayed as a colored bar with no numeric value for screen-reader users.
Adding twenty teammates requires reopening the invite dialog for every address.
Clearing one filter resets my sort order and page size too.
The export button is placed next to Delete with the same icon weight.
The dashboard abbreviates every product area, and several abbreviations are identical.
There is no visible difference between an AI summary and the original customer text.
The required CSV date format appears only after the upload fails.
I have to open each item to learn why it was sent for human review.
The workspace switcher truncates organization names to the same first twelve characters.
Search chips use color alone to indicate whether they include or exclude a term.
The integration error message says “request failed” but gives no next step.
Weekly and monthly charts use different colors for the same sentiment.
Review notes are hidden in a collapsed section even when another reviewer mentioned me.
Column detection is accurate, but the preview is too narrow to verify long responses.
The model explanation is written like API documentation instead of plain language.
Permission errors appear only after a guest completes the whole invite form.
Saved searches are ordered by creation date with no way to pin frequently used ones.
I cannot tell whether an export contains the current filter or all feedback.
The chart tooltip covers the exact data point I am trying to compare.
After editing a label, focus jumps to the top and I lose my place in the queue.
The import page calls rejected rows “skipped,” which sounds intentional rather than erroneous.
Urgency and negative sentiment use nearly identical badges, so reviewers confuse them.
Does the importer keep blank rows or discard them?
What happens to an item if the model returns invalid JSON?
Can two reviewers work on the same queue without overwriting each other?
How is negative percentage calculated when sentiment is Mixed?
Why does searching “login error” return praise mentioning successful login?
Can an organization member belong to more than one workspace?
Do scheduled exports include feedback added after the schedule was created?
What encoding should we use for feedback written in Hindi?
Is confidence calibrated, or is it only the model’s own estimate?
Who can see the reason I entered for overriding a category?
Can I download the records behind a dashboard chart?
How do I remove a saved filter without deleting the shared version?
Where are submitter email addresses stored, and who can view them?
Does the Slack integration retry messages when Slack is unavailable?
Can I import a CSV without a header row?
What label should I use for feedback that contains both a bug and a request?
How long do completed items remain in the review history?
Does the trend chart use submission time or classification time?
Can search handle misspellings, or does it require an exact word?
How can I transfer organization ownership before leaving the company?
Which fields are sent to Slack when a critical alert fires?
Why are five rows listed as rejected when the file preview looked valid?
Can I see the raw model response for a classification error?
What should a reviewer do when category is clear but product area is not?
Importing our historical survey file worked perfectly on the first try.
The summaries are concise and have not hidden the customer’s actual complaint.
The side-by-side original text made reviewing an uncertain label very easy.
Product-area trends helped us defend the roadmap with evidence instead of anecdotes.
Saved filters make our Monday triage routine much more consistent.
Adding a guest reviewer took less than a minute and exposed only the right workspace.
The export matched every active filter, including the date range.
The rejected-row download made fixing our source file painless.
I appreciate that low confidence creates a review task instead of pretending to be correct.
Review history clearly shows who changed the category and why.
The dashboard loads quickly even with our full year of feedback.
Search highlighting makes it easy to verify why each result matched.
Switching organizations feels safe because the workspace name remains visible everywhere.
Zendesk sync recovered from an outage without creating duplicate tickets.
The column mapper understood our oddly named survey export immediately.
The category definitions are clear enough that our reviewers usually agree with the model.
Bulk accept saved us an hour while still preserving the review log.
The sentiment chart helped us catch a gradual decline before support volume spiked.
Sharing a filtered view made our handoff to support much cleaner.
The permission summary answered every access question before we sent invites.
Scheduled exports arrive on time and use predictable filenames.
The import status messages are the clearest I have seen in a feedback tool.
The system admitted it could not classify a vague response, which increased my trust.
Everything from ingestion to review feels connected instead of like separate tools.
